newsitem.title: USA: Minor Metals Inc criticizes Stockpile cobalt bid.
newsitem.headline: Minor Metals Inc criticizes Stockpile cobalt bid.

text.p: Cobalt trader, Minor Metals Inc, on Thursday expressed reservations about the "draft solicitation" proposed by the U.S. Defense National Stockpile Center (Stockpile) for cobalt sales, saying the proposal does not specifiy parameters that are subject to negotiation.
The Stockpile's draft proposal establishes the valuation factors in descending order of importance: unit price, payment terms, and removal schedule.
In the previous negotiated solicitation in March, all terms were open to negotiation.
But Minor Metals Inc launched a lawsuit against the Stockpile in March, alleging the government agency cheated the company out of the sale of 1.1 million pounds of cobalt.
The U.S. District ruled in favor of the Stockpile.

"As the DNSC well knows the parameters and evaluations procedures in government contracts should be made known to all offerors, so that offerors may structure their proposals to maximize their value to the government," said Rami Weisfisch, president of Minor Metals in an open letter to the cobalt industry, presented at an industry meeting held by the Stockpile in Virginia.
"Offerors cannot provide the government with the contract terms that are most advantageous to the government if they do not know what the government values," he said.

"This language (in the draft solicitation) does not provide enough information to allow the offerors to structure their proposals in the manner that will maximize their value to the government and thus is not scrupulously fair."
Richard Connelly, administrator of the Stockpile, declined to comment specifically on Weisfisch's remarks, but he said "our response will be the final solicitation."
Lacking any exchange-based trading, Stockpile "sealed bid" sales are the only transparent forum for pricing cobalt, traders said.
In the new format of "negotiated bids", only a rough estimate of total value and quantities sold are given by the Stockpile.
The latest Stockpile proposal calls for the sale of 1.5 million pounds of cobalt. The deadline for bids is August 29. ((Derek Caney, New York Commodities Desk, 212-859-1646))
